evals.name: quick-chat-target-up
evals.prompt: I need a fake OpenAI-compatible LLM server running locally so I can hit /v1/chat/completions with curl and get a streaming response back. Get one up and confirm it's actually serving.
evals.expected_output: Builds/launches aiperf-mock-server with --fast and --no-tokenizer, binds 127.0.0.1, verifies via /health and/or a real /v1/chat/completions curl, and confirms liveness rather than assuming it booted.
assertions: Launched aiperf-mock-server with --no-tokenizer to avoid a Hugging Face download
Used --fast (or otherwise chose an instant-latency mode) for a quick smoke target
Actively verified the server responded (a successful /health curl or a real /v1/chat/completions response) rather than assuming it booted

evals.name: realistic-latency-for-aiperf
evals.prompt: I want to run `aiperf profile` against a local stand-in inference server that has realistic latency — something like 45ms to first token and 8ms per output token. Set the server up and show me the aiperf command to benchmark it.
evals.expected_output: Launches aiperf-mock-server WITHOUT --fast, sets --ttft 45 and --itl 8, uses 127.0.0.1, and gives an aiperf profile command pointing --url at the mock with --model and --endpoint-type chat --streaming.
assertions: Launched aiperf-mock-server WITHOUT --fast, so realistic latency is retained
Set first-token latency to 45ms (--ttft 45 or MOCK_SERVER_TTFT=45)
Set inter-token latency to 8ms (--itl 8 or MOCK_SERVER_ITL=8)
Gave an aiperf profile command pointing --url/-u at http://127.0.0.1:<port>
aiperf command includes a model (--model/-m) and --endpoint-type chat with --streaming

evals.name: start-verify-list-endpoints
evals.prompt: Start the rust mock inference server from this repo, make sure it's really up (not just that the command returned), and then tell me which HTTP endpoints it exposes.
evals.expected_output: Launches aiperf-mock-server, does an active liveness check against /health on 127.0.0.1, and enumerates real routes (chat/completions, embeddings, rerank, tgi, metrics, etc.) grounded in the actual server.
assertions: Performed an active liveness check against /health on 127.0.0.1
Did not report 'running' from mere command return — confirmed an actual HTTP response
Enumerated real routes grounded in the server: /v1/chat/completions plus at least 3 others (e.g. embeddings, rerank, tgi generate, metrics)
